summary: 9remote exposes installer shell over Cloudflare tunnel
details: The package server opens an interactive PTY (bash/zsh/cmd/pwsh via node-pty) on the installer's host and proxies input from WebSocket messages arriving through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel brokered via 9remote.cc. Frames tagged as "input" are written verbatim to the PTY (case "input": b.pty.write(s.data)), giving any remote client that presents a valid pair key a full interactive shell on the host. Access is gated only by a short-lived QR pair key (roughly a 30-minute window); once paired, arbitrary command execution on the installer's machine is available to the remote peer. The dist/cli.cjs and dist/server.cjs modules perform outbound POSTs to the tunnel broker and orchestrate the WebSocket-to-PTY path. A postinstall step also spawns `npm install systray2@2.1.4 --no-save` into ~/.9remote/runtime/ to fetch a tray helper; this fetch is version-pinned against the default npm registry and is not itself the concerning behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
